title: Korea In January: What To Pack And Do
summary: Planning a January trip to Korea? Learn how Seoul’s cold compares with Busan, what to pack, and what to see after snowfall.

slides.title: January: Pack For Seoul's Cold
slides.sub: Seoul days often stay below freezing.
slides.voice: Korea in January? Pack for Seoul's below-freezing days.

slides.title: The South Is Milder
slides.sub: Busan averages about eight degrees by day.
slides.voice: Busan averages around eight degrees by day, far milder than Seoul.

slides.title: Layer Up And Grip
slides.sub: Bring waterproof shoes with good grip.
slides.voice: Wear a long padded coat, thermal layers, and grippy waterproof shoes.

slides.title: Check Festival Dates
slides.voice: Gangwon's ice festivals offer trout fishing; dates depend on safe ice.

slides.title: Go Early After Snow
slides.sub: Visit before footprints mark the snow.
slides.voice: After snowfall, visit Gyeongbokgung early, before the snow gets trampled.
